findings.title: All app modules are still eagerly imported at module initialization time
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, the `appStore` object properties are assigned the result of calling `import("./...")` directly (e.g., `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")`) rather than functions that call `import()` on demand (e.g., `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`). Because every `import()` expression in the object literal is evaluated immediately when `packages/app-store/index.ts` is loaded, importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers loading all 28 app packages at once instead of lazily importing only the requested app when accessed.

findings.title: Unawaited async `forEach` prevents recurring calendar deletions from being awaited in `apiDeletes`
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring event (lines 458-470), `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { ... })` awaits `getCalendar(credential)` and `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` before calling `apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent)`. Because `forEach` does not wait for `async` callbacks, execution proceeds to `await apiDeletes` (line 617) and `await Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) before the `forEach` callbacks have pushed their promises into `apiDeletes` or completed deleting the calendar events. Use a `for...of` loop (as done on lines 480-483) or `Promise.all` with `.map` so the deletions are tracked in `apiDeletes` and awaited.

findings.title: Async `forEach` inside `try/catch` does not await deletions and leaks unhandled rejections
findings.body: On lines 124-139, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is wrapped in a `try / catch` block. Because `forEach` ignores the Promise returned by an `async` callback, `Reschedule` does not wait for `getCalendar`, `calendar?.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` to finish before returning, and any error thrown or rejected inside the callback will become an unhandled promise rejection rather than being caught by the surrounding `try / catch`. Replace `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.

findings.title: Async `forEach` inside `try/catch` does not await deletions and leaks unhandled rejections
findings.body: On lines 124-139, `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` is wrapped in a `try / catch` block. Because `forEach` ignores the Promise returned by an `async` callback, `Reschedule` does not wait for `getCalendar`, `calendar?.deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` to finish before returning, and any error thrown or rejected inside the callback will bypass the `try / catch` block as an unhandled promise rejection. Replace `forEach` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))`.

findings.title: Unawaited async `forEach` in `requestReschedule` discards calendar and video deletion promises
findings.body: In `requestReschedule` (lines 553-567), `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... })` awaits `getCalendar` and returns the promises from `calendar?.deleteEvent` and `deleteMeeting` to `forEach`, which ignores them. As a result, `calendar?.deleteEvent` is no longer even started synchronously, the mutation resolves without waiting for calendar events or video meetings to be deleted, and any rejection in `getCalendar`, `deleteEvent`, or `deleteMeeting` goes unhandled. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => { ... }))` instead.
